en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section Third Chapter
Discussion on the One Being Liberated: Is that which is liberated the same as that which is being liberated?
Yes, it is.
“Is it partially liberated and partially unliberated?
“One should not say so…” [as before] … “Is it partially liberated and partially unliberated?”
“Yes.

“In one respect he is a stream-enterer; in one respect he is not a stream-enterer. In one respect he has attained, acquired, reached, realized, and dwells having entered upon the fruit of stream-entry;
he dwells having touched it with his body, yet in one respect he does not dwell having touched it with his body.”
Having touched [the fruit], he dwells [therein]; in one respect, he is one who returns for seven times at most, one who goes from family to family, or a one-seeder;

he is endowed with verified confidence in the Buddha, [and so on] in the Dhamma …pe… in the Saṅgha …pe… he is endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, yet in one respect he is not endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that one part is liberated and one part is not liberated? Yes.
Is it the case that one part is a once-returner, one part is not a once-returner; and that one part has attained, acquired, reached, realized, and entered upon the fruit of once-returning,
dwelling having touched it with the body, while another part does not dwell having touched it with the body?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it the case that one part is liberated and one part is not liberated? Yes.
In one respect he is a non-returner; in one respect he is not a non-returner. In one respect he has attained, acquired, reached, realized, and dwells having entered upon the fruit of non-returning;
he dwells having touched it with his body, and in one respect he does not dwell having touched it with his body.
In one respect he is one who attains final nibbāna in the interval, one who attains final nibbāna upon landing, or one who attains final nibbāna without exertion.
"One who attains final nibbāna with exertion, one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm, and one who is not in every respect one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm"?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
"Is it that one part is liberated and one part is not liberated?"
“Yes.
“In one respect the Arahant is an Arahant, and in another respect he is not an Arahant;

in one respect he has attained, acquired, reached, realized, and entered upon and dwells in the state of Arahantship, having touched it with his body, and in another respect he does not dwell having touched it with his body.”

"Is it not the case that one part has become free from lust, free from hatred, and free from delusion … [and so on] … one part of what is to be realized has been realized, while one part of what is to be realized has not been realized?
"One should certainly not say so … [and so on]."
Is that which is liberated [already] being liberated? Yes.
Is it liberated at the moment of arising and being liberated at the moment of dissolution? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that "the liberated is being liberated"?
“Yes, that is so.
“Is it not said by the Blessed One:

‘For one who knows thus and sees thus, the mind is liberated from the taint of sensual desire, the mind is liberated from the taint of existence, and the mind is liberated from the taint of ignorance’?”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it must be said—
“‘The liberated and that which is being liberated’— is it the case that there is what is liberated and what is being liberated?”—
Yes, it is.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One:

“When his mind is thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, stainless, free from defilements, become supple, wieldy, steady, and attained to imperturbability, he directs his mind toward the knowledge of the destruction of the taints”?
Is this indeed the Suttanta?
“Yes, [it is so].
Therefore, it should not be said:
“the liberated is being liberated.”
Is there a mind that is being liberated?
Yes. Is there a mind that is becoming lustful, becoming hateful, becoming deluded, and becoming defiled? Yes.

It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it not the case that there is both passion and non-passion, both hatred and non-hatred, both delusion and non-delusion, both what is cut and what is uncut, both what is split and what is unsplit, and both what is done and what is undone? Yes, it is.

If there is both what is lustful and what is not lustful, what is hateful and what is not hateful, what is deluded and what is not deluded, what is cut off and what is not cut off, what is broken and what is not broken, and what is done and what is not done, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
"There is a consciousness being liberated.
The Discussion on Consciousness Being Liberated is finished.
